description: Serve an app under the owner's own domain (Pro: three domains per account, subdomains included: app.example.com and blog.example.com count as one domain, example.com; at most 10 hostnames per account). 'attach' with a hostname (e.g. app.example.com, 64 characters at most) answers the DNS record the owner must add (CNAME to clients.dropyour.site) and the state 'en_attente'; the domain serves once the DNS points to Dropyour and the certificate is issued ('actif'). 'status' re-checks it and returns the domain, the removed domains that still redirect ('removed'), how many domains are used ('domaines': used and max; 'quota' carries the same two numbers) and how many hostnames ('noms': used and max, the removed names that still redirect included); when something blocks, 'raison' says why (delai, bloque, caa, dns_parti, certificat_inactif, verification_impossible). 'detach' removes the domain without breaking any link: the name keeps its certificate and redirects to the app's dropyour.site address as long as the owner's DNS points to Dropyour, and it no longer counts as a domain (it still counts as a hostname while it redirects). You can detach on your own, no human confirmation: the activity shows your name on the line, and the owner can put it back for 30 days. To put it back yourself, 'attach' the same hostname to the same app within 30 days: it comes back as it was. While a removed name still redirects, only its owner (and, after a transfer, the previous owner) can attach it again. A refusal carries a reason code in parentheses (nom_invalide, nom_plateforme, trop_long, sans_pro, deja_rattache, app_a_un_domaine, quota, quota_noms, redirige_ailleurs, nom_indisponible, cloudflare_indisponible). 'quota': the hostname would open one domain more than the account has (a subdomain of a domain already attached is never refused this way). 'quota_noms': the account already holds its 10 hostnames. Needs a connected account.
name: dropyour_domain
title: Custom domain of an app
